tender.title: Home Safety and Security Installation Service
tender.description:
Short Description:Kent County Council is undertaking preliminary market engagement on Tuesday 25 August 10:00-11.30 and Friday 4 September 10:00-11.30, to inform the future development of its Home Safety and Security Installation Service. 
We are inviting organisations to attend an online market engagement event to help inform the future design and commissioning of the service.
The online sessions will be facilitated by Kent County Council and will include a presentation on the proposed service requirements, opportunities for discussion through facilitated group conversations, and interactive feedback activities to gather provider views and market intelligence.
This exercise is being conducted to:
•understand current market delivery models for domestic abuse sanctuary-style provision,
•gather insight on service design, delivery approaches, and capacity, and
•help shape potential future commissioning arrangements.
The Council is keen to engage with organisations that have experience of delivering property security and target hardening interventions within domestic settings. This includes providers with expertise in assessing, supplying, and installing security measures that help individuals remain safely in their own homes.
We are particularly interested in organisations that can deliver services in a professional, discreet, and trauma-informed manner. Experience of working with victim-survivors, vulnerable residents, or households experiencing safeguarding concerns will be beneficial.
Organisations from the domestic abuse, housing, community safety, safeguarding, and property security sectors are encouraged to participate. Providers with experience of partnership working across statutory and voluntary sector services, including housing, community safety, safeguarding, and domestic abuse agencies, will be well placed to contribute to discussions on future service delivery.
The Council is inviting organisations to contribute to this engagement to help:
•inform the development of the service model,
•understand different approaches to delivering sanctuary-style services,
•explore delivery options, including partnership models,
•review eligibility criteria and referral pathways, and
•assess market capacity and interest in delivering such a service.
This engagement will support the Council in developing an appropriate procurement approach and ensuring a fair and competitive process.
To express your interest in attending, or ask any questions about the online event, please email domesticabusecommissioning@kent.gov.uk by Friday 21 August. 
Kent County Council intend to procure Home Safety and Security Installation Service through a tender process. 
This procurement will be conducted in accordance with the new Procurement Act 2023. Please note this notice is not a call for competition; therefore, attendees are not expected to submit any documents at this stage. 
Further information relating to this procurement will be published on Central Digital Platform and the Kent Business Portal at a future date. Interested providers are advised to create a supplier profile on the Kent Business Portal to receive notifications about the future procurement opportunity, once the formal tender is launched
The estimated contract value is up to £500,000 per annum. 
Any financial information provided at this stage is indicative only and subject to change following completion of market engagement and internal approvals.
Estimated contract length is 3 years with the option to extend for a further 2 years, at this stage this is indicative only and subject to change following completion of market engagement and internal approvals.

lots.description:
This is a pre-qualification activity in advance of a formal tender process.
ScotRail requires a Service Provider (SP) to provide the Lease of high-performance industrial pressure washer systems suitable for cleaning railway rolling stock and depot infrastructure. The system will be installed outside the maintenance sheds, with small delivery stations with hoses inside the shed. The water will be supplied via fixed piping into the shed, the electrical connection will be supplied as well as concrete base for the machine to be sited. The supplier will be responsible for providing detail to attach to the pressure washer equipment.
We require a quantity of 9 Pressure washers across 5 ScotRail depots/locations: Corkerhill (1), Eastfield (1), Haymarket (4), Inverness (1) and Shields (2).
The reliability and availability of pressure washers is of high importance to the on-going maintenance activities at depots and as such the requirement of asset technology refresh, economy principles and long term sustainability is vital which will also assist with our commitment to ISO standards and continual improvement. A proven structure for on-going renewal and upgrade to ensure the machine is always highly performing and reliable to the end user.
Our preference is for a “Circular model” type solution (A circular model is an economic system designed to eliminate waste, keep materials in use, and regenerate natural systems, built around three core principles: eliminate waste and pollution, circulate products and materials, and regenerate nature).
General
Location: Outdoor installation adjacent to the railway maintenance shed at the 5 depots as above.
Application: Cleaning of train exteriors, bogies, underframes, and shed floors and pits.
Operation: Capable of frequent daily use in a heavy-duty industrial environment.
Compliance: Must comply with UK health, safety, and environmental regulations.
Background Information on our existing arrangements.
The depots require a safe and reliable system for pressure washing activities.
There is currently a variety of equipment at each depot which this system will look to replace.
Fixed pressure washer kits within the sheds, varying in ages and condition.
Fixed pressure washer kits out-with sheds or held in plant rooms varying in ages and conditions.
Industrial portable pressure washers which can be moved from building to building, most kit is well used and older.
Small local pressure washer kits due to use don’t have a long life span.
The portable kit has lengthy cables, hoses and/or is fuelled by diesel and then transported around site enhancing manual handling risk, safety risk due to hot exhausts, environmental risk with moving fuel round.
See PQQ document at ScotRail link above for further details.

tender.description:
Norwich City Council was awarded UK government's Levelling Up Fund (LUF) to deliver improvements to Sloughbottom Park.   The project is centred on health and wellbeing, aiming to improve the park accessibility and amenities for all users, supporting more people to live healthier and more active lifestyles from a young age. 
This construction project will deliver a linked set of new community and sporting facilities, including:
•	A new Sports Hub designed to Sport England and Football Foundation standards which will include new changing facilities, including fully accessible facilities; changing places toilet; multi use studio; refreshment outlet and associated office reception and storage facilities
•	Full refurbishment of existing Pavilion to provide a new café facility, public WCs and a community use room, to serve park users.

lots.title: Segmentation
lots.description:
AHDB uses consumer segmentation to underpin AHDB strategy and inform marketing activities. The segmentation is based on actual purchasing behaviour and attitudes with a focus on red meat and dairy categories. The segmentation allows AHDB to have a common ‘language’ for all sectors and a way of targeting consumers more efficiently, beyond just simple demographics. 
The current segmentation was developed in 2025 and is key to helping target shoppers within current AHDB marketing campaigns. Regular updates on the purchasing behaviour of the segments are carried out to monitor any changes across segments.
AHDB would like to maintain the regular updates of the purchasing behaviour for the current segments from April 2027 to April 2029.
AHDB would also like the option to either refresh the current segmentation or create a new segmentation within the next 5 years depending on market conditions.
The segmentation is based on an extensive range of questions covering grocery shopping habits, attitudes to food, health and nutrition, cooking, sustainability, animal welfare, meat/dairy and household dietary requirements. Agencies must outline a suitable methodology to reproduce this segmentation if required. AHDB can provide the questions and coding that is used the current segmentation.
Maintenance to provide regular updates on purchase behaviour for total market and split for current segments. This will also require profiling and allocation to segments for any new panellists.
The basic measures required will consist of the following as a minimum:
• Value
• Volume
• Price
• Buyer numbers i.e. penetration
• Volume per buyer i.e. frequency and volume per trip
Data must be split by retailers including the following as a minimum:
• Tesco
• Sainsbury’s
• Asda
• Morrisons
• Aldi
• Lidl
• Co-op
• Waitrose
• Iceland
• M&S
• Ocado
• Independents & Symbols
AHDB require a proposal to best meet AHDB’s specification with a budget of approximately:
- £38,000 per annum including VAT for maintaining the current segmentation,
AHDB doesn’t have a fixed budget for other areas or future years, please refer to the Specification for further information.

lots.title: Marketing mix models
lots.description:
AHDB’s marketing team have done a few consumer media measure studies over previous years. They use this information to communicate the success of campaigns to our levy payers and show the return to retail sales our campaigns have for our sector products. We also use this information to inform future campaign activity and look to optimise based on recommendations from the results of the analysis.
AHDB currently has two marketing campaigns – Let’s Eat Balanced which covers lamb, beef and dairy and Love Pork which covers Pork.  
AHDB would require potential analysis for campaign results from top level categories like total beef and lamb, total pigmeat or total dairy down to specific cuts or products such as pork medallions or cow’s milk.
KPIs required: 
Return to retail sales for every £1 spent on campaign advertising
• Spend uplift due to the campaign
• Volume uplift due to the campaign
• Number of lapsed shoppers re-engaged
• If lapsed shoppers were retained
• Campaign reach (% households) 
• Response curves for likelihood to purchase
Data will be used by staff of AHDB insight teams and marketing teams. The data must be available for regular Levy Board publication purposes including web publications.
AHDB expects the following client service activities to be included within the data cost:
• Training and technical support/help for all users for software programmes.
• Any data checking or sign off required by the supplier
Suppliers should outline details and experience of any 3rd party agencies that will be used to deliver the research project, clearly indicating the stage in which they would be involved.
Further optional services to be made available include:
- Ad hoc data requests beyond the scope of the online tool
AHDB require a proposal to best meet AHDB’s specification with a maximum budget for all core and optional extras of £100,000 per mix model including VAT 
For further details, please refer to the Specification.

lots.title: Adhoc panel insight
lots.description:
AHDB occasionally does ad hoc projects which require panel data. This lot will allow us to be flexible and react to changing markets or differing levy payer needs.
HDB are looking for options for an agency to do bespoke ad hoc analysis using panel data. These will include but are not limited to:
1) Nutritional data (especially Nutrient profile modelling (NPM)) 
AHDB is keen to look at nutrition data and see how we can support the meat and dairy industry to be healthier – especially if mandatory reporting of basket NPM comes in. This could be looking at specific categories or by looking through a retailer lens. Details should be given on methodology for NPM calculation including possibility for reporting on NPM 2004 and NPM 2018.
Alongside the NPM, AHDB may wish to see other nutritional table data such as fibre content, protein content, calories etc. 
a. Nutrition data for 5 categories such as primary red meat, primary poultry, meat-free, cows milk etc. 
b. Nutrition data for 10 subcategories and cuts such as beef steaks, lamb ready meals, pork sausages, cheddar cheese, Greek yogurt etc. 
c. Nutrition data for 5 basket types such as basket containing primary red meat, basket containing primary fish etc.
d. Nutrition scores for baskets by all major retailers such as Tesco, Sainsburys, Aldi etc. please detail which retailers are robust.
2) Basket analysis 
AHDB may wish to understand what other categories are in the basket when red meat or dairy are also present. Details should be given to the level of other categories in the basket which can be analysed.
a. Data on the percentage likelihood of other categories from total grocery, shoppers are buying if they purchase other products in the basket
b. Data on the volume and spend of total grocery categories within a basket
There is no fixed or agreed budget for these projects and will vary through the length of the contract.
For further details, please refer to the Specification

tender.title: Portsmouth International Port - Repairs & Maintenance Support Staff and Ancillary Services
tender.description:
Portsmouth International Port (the 'Port'), a directorate of Portsmouth City Council (the 'Council'), is seeking to appoint a Contractor to provide a dedicated core maintenance team and associated gas maintenance services across the Port estate. The contract is expected to have an annual value in the region of £400,000 to £450,000. The contract will be awarded for an initial term of three (3) years, with the option to extend for up to a further two (2) years, up to a maximum total contract term of five (5) years.
The scope of the service includes the provision of a dedicated on-site maintenance team to undertake planned, minor and corrective maintenance activities across the Port estate, together with the provision of gas safety inspections, planned gas maintenance, reactive repairs and an out-of-hours emergency call-out service. The Contractor may also be required to provide quotations for additional works and specialist trades as required. This procurement represents a re-procurement of the Council's existing repairs and maintenance service provision
Background information
Portsmouth International Port
The Port is wholly owned by the Council and is the UK's largest municipal port. The Port is a major UK port, responsible for handling millions of passengers and vital cargo across the globe. With easy access from the motorway and major shipping lanes, the Port is ideally placed for ferries, cruise, and freight. 
Within Portsmouth Cruise and Ferry Port, referred to as the port, there are five Roll On/Roll Off berths serving both ferries and cruise ships. The ferries provide regular sailings to France, Spain, and the Channel Islands; the cruise ships attend the port with both full turnaround and cruise calls. Within the year of 2025, the Port welcomed 1.6 million cruise and ferry passengers, 570,000 passenger vehicles, and 190,000 fright units. 
The port usually operates during the hours of 0530 to midnight, 7 days a week, 52 weeks of the year. It has bold environmental ambitions to tackle its emissions and carbon footprint and aims to reach carbon zero by 2050. The Port's plans to improve air quality and their carbon footprint can be found under Sustainability and innovation on the Port's website at Sustainability and innovation - Portsmouth Port (portsmouth-port.co.uk). 
Further information about the port, including an overview of the facilities, current ferry and cruise schedules, cargo and logistics, etc, can be freely accessed on the Port's website via the weblink Home - Portsmouth Port (portsmouth-port.co.uk) 
The Port manages The Camber, which is set close to the harbour entrance and is Portsmouth's oldest commercial docks, comprising of four berths that are available for small vessels that are primarily local fishing boats, small coastal commercial vessels, and private pleasure craft. The Port is also responsible for a significant area of the land in this area. Further information can be found on the Port's website at The Camber - Portsmouth Port (portsmouthport.co.uk).
Future Requirements - Core Team
The successful contractor is to supply a permanent core team of staff to supplement the Port's own directly employed Technical Services Group who carry out repairs and maintenance across the Port's estate. Both teams are directed by the Port's directly employed Maintenance and Facilities Manager to undertake planned, minor, and corrective maintenance.
One member of the core team of staff should act as a working supervisor having a good understanding of the Port's requirement and undertaking day to day liaison with the Port's Maintenance and Facilities Manager.
The core team are on site at the Port between Monday - Friday (excluding bank holidays), between the hours 8:00 - 17:00. Due to the operational requirements and security at the Port consistency of staffing is required and members of the permanent core team of staff should be treated as a dedicated resource. 
To cater for the dynamic work requirements, it is envisaged that the contractors' staff will be required to carry out a range of different jobs, which includes a range of trades (this is not an exhaustive list): 
•	Carpentry 
•	Plumbing 
•	Decorations / Painting 
•	Groundwork 
•	Horticultural 
On occasion the Contractor may be requested by the Port's Maintenance and Facilities Manager to provide a fixed quotation for a particular job or to provide additional trades outside of those listed above.
The Contractor will provide a call out facility to make safe, prevent further damage to property or personnel and to safeguard the public within a maximum of two hours 
Commercial Gas Services

Local Government Review 
As part of the wider Local Government Review (LGR), Portsmouth City Council has been required to work with neighbouring authorities to support the development of future local government structures and governance arrangements. Under the confirmed proposals, Portsmouth City Council will become part of a new unitary authority covering the areas of Portsmouth, Gosport, Fareham and Havant, together with Newlands, Horndean, Clanfield and Rowlands Castle. The new authority is expected to assume responsibility for local authority services from 1 April 2028.
Portsmouth International Port is a distinct operational asset owned and managed by Portsmouth City Council. Canon Street Changing Places Toilet Project – Pre-Market Engagement 
Background 
Taunton Town Council (TTC) has taken over from Somerset Council a number of the public toilets within Taunton and is undertaking a phased programme to refurbish some of these facilities. 
TTC has existing Changing Places units at Paul Street and Tower Street in Taunton and is looking to install a third unit at our Canon Street toilets facility. 
The main refurbishment of the Canon Street toilets was completed in 2025 with space being left for the installation of a Changing Places toilet. 
Over the past year TTC has undertaken a detailed review and consultation exercise in relation to Changing Places toilets and their supporting arrangements.  This review actively sought and obtained input from Disabled people as the users of these facilities.   
The review concluded that in addition to providing the specific Changing Places equipment we also need to provide: 
Access controls by way of CAME KMS key fob backed up by an online registration process in order to provide secure access and to protect the facilities from vandalism and anti-social behaviour 
A monitored emergency alarm and response service provided in conjunction with the Somerset Council Lifeline team 
Fire alarms linked to the key fob Mag Lock to provide for automatic door release 
Accessible and clear signage to cover all aspects of the facility 
Up to date, clear and accessible information on our and other relevant websites 
Engagement with Disabled people when designing these facilities to ensure that we get it right 
Proposed timeline 
Ideally, the Council is looking to have the procurement exercise completed and a contract agreed by the end of February 2027 for the works to be completed and the facility open by May 2027. 
Purpose of the pre-market engagement 
The review we have undertaken has, as detailed above, indicated that there is far more to providing a Changing Places facility than just installing standard Changing Places toilet equipment. 
In practice we need to think holistically about the entire user experience and engage with users when designing and implementing these facilities. 
So, for the Canon Street project we want to procure a complete solution which also delivers in addition to the standard Changing Places equipment the supporting technology i.e. the access controls, monitored emergency alarm equipment, fire alarm / Mag Lock auto unlocking, signage, Building Control approvals etc. 
Ideally, the Council wants to engage a single main contractor to oversee and manage all aspects of the installation including any enabling minor structural, electrical or plumbing works required to the unit to facilitate the installation of the Changing Places equipment. 
However, before progressing to a formal procurement we are interested in understanding whether this approach (i.e. the single contractor) is realistic and will generate competitive bids. 
More detail is provided below in relation to the specific requirements. 
Overall objectives of the project 
The overall objective of this project is to provide a quality Changing Places toilet facility with the additional supporting technology and approach outlined above. 
Summary of the specific requirements 
More specifically we are looking for the: 
Completion of any and all minor enabling works required to enable the installation to comply with the Changing Places requirements and to enable the installation of the CAME KMS key fob, emergency and fire alarms.  (This includes changes to enable the existing door to work with a CAME KMS key fob and to provide a paddle handle locking mechanism or the provision and installation of a new door, if required)  
Provision and installation of quality Changing Places equipment to Changing Places Consortium standards including a wash/dry toilet 
Provision, installation and commissioning of a CAME KMS key fob access control system which is integrated with our existing Simplekey Web software 
Installation in conjunction with the Somerset Council Lifeline team of their emergency alarm monitoring equipment and wireless alarm cords.  (NB.  We would expect the contractor to liaise directly with the Somerset Lifeline team regarding any enabling electrical work required to enable them to install their alarm equipment) 
Provision, installation and commissioning of an open protocol fire alarm in the Changing Places unit and utility area, which is to be linked to the key fob Mag Lock to provide for auto release in the event of an alarm 
The provision and installation of quality (i.e. acrylic or aluminium) instruction signs in respect of each element of the Changing Places equipment.  (NB.  TTC will provide all other signage) 
Questions for potential suppliers 
Would you be happy and able to provide a competitive bid for the full scope of the work outlined above?  If not, please indicate which areas would cause particular difficulty. 
Are there any key elements that you believe we are missing?  If so, please specify what they are. 
Is our proposed timetable realistic? 
Would you be interested in bidding for this?

tender.description:
18 THE SCHEME IN BRIEF
18.1 Christmas lights decorate the town centre for the Christmas period extending from the switch on event to 6th January each year. The existing scheme comprises LED icicle cross street lights and hedgehog motif frame cross street lights attached to catenary wire installations in the town centre and 12 column lights along Wilton Road.
18.2 The erection and decoration of the lights on the town Christmas Tree in the Market Square and the Christmas Tree on Brookend Street and their removal in early January.
18.3 The Market House is also decorated with icicle LED lights and these will form part of the scheme.
18.4 Christmas lights on three trees on Gloucester Road.
19 COLLECTION
19.1 The lights are currently in storage and the Contractor shall arrange collection.
20 MAINTENANCE
20.1 Prior to installation, all eye bolts supporting catenary wires and catenary wires shall be inspected annually and this is to be carried out by a qualified contractor to test the condition of the support brackets and eyebolts to confirm that up to a maximum weight of 6kN can be supported on the wires. All testing must be compliant with BS8539. The Council must receive a copy of the eyebolt test certificate and will be responsible for payment for the replacement or repair of any eyebolts or catenary wires, but the testing costs should be included in this tender. Any work (which must be first authorised in writing by the Council), shall be carried out by a qualified contractor.
20.2 All street lighting columns that have Christmas lights attached need a Structural Test Certificate in place. All testing needs to be compliant with BSEN40.
20.2 All LED lights will be checked by a qualified contractor and PAT tested annually to ensure that they are fit for purpose. The Council must receive a copy of any test certificate and will be responsible for payment for the replacement or repair of any lights, but the testing should be included in this tender. Any work (which must be first authorised in writing by the Council), shall be carried out by a qualified contractor.
20.3 All 'black boxes' which provide power to the lights needs a valid EICR certificate. All testing must be compliant with BS7671. The Council must receive a copy of any EICR test certificate and will be responsible for payment for the replacement or repair of any boxes, but the testing should be included in this tender. Any work (which must be first authorised in writing by the Council), shall be carried out by a qualified contractor.
20.4 The lights must be maintained during the period they are on display. A scheduled inspection of the display is required to ensure everything is functioning correctly and to attend to any minor faults. In addition, a call out of no more than 24 hours is required for major faults including, but not limited to, complete failure of light string, Christmas tree light failure, damage caused through vandalism, storms or road traffic accidents. If there is a charge for call outs this must be stated in the quotation.
21 INSTALLATION
21.1 Installation of lights shall be carried out at a mutually agreed date prior to switch on event but it must be no later than one week (full 7 days) prior to the notified switch on date each year.
21.2 The Contractor must adhere to the relevant codes of practice and statutory regulations. In particular the erection, testing and maintenance of the installation must be carried out in accordance with the latest Wiring Regulations (BS 7671) determined by the IET and undertaken by a competent person as laid out in those regulations.
22 REMOVAL AND STORAGE
22.1 Lights will be switched off no later than 6th January each year.
22.2 Lights will be removed as soon as possible after and as close as possible to 6th January.
22.3 After removal the lights will be stored by the Contractor in a covered, secure location. The location to be notified to the Council and the appropriate insurance will be sought to cover loss or damage. A certificate of proof of insurance will be required.
22.4 The Contractor is required to give a short written statement after the completion of the annual display outlining any issues, the need for replacement lights and suggestions for improvements for the coming year.

procedure.features:
Competitive Flexible Procedure designed as a two-stage tender process. 
Stage 1 – Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ)
Stage 2 – Invitation to Tender (ITT)

criteria.description:
The PSQ will be evaluated in two stages: 
a.	Stage 1 (PASS / FAIL Evaluation) – Qualification Envelope. The Qualification Envelope contains PASS / FAIL questions which must be achieve a PASS by the Potential Provider in order to progress to the Stage 2 (except where the Authority has discretion not to fail the Potential Provider).
b.	Stage 2 (SCORED and PASS / FAIL Evaluation) – Technical Envelope. Those Potential Providers who are successful in the Stage 1 evaluation will then be taken forward into the Stage 2 evaluation where their capability will be assessed using a series of PASS/FAIL and weighted questions which include a scoring regime across a range of weighted criteria. The weighted questions and criteria have been weighted to reflect the relevant importance of the question and criteria to the assessment of the capability of the Potential Provider. 
No more than five Potential Providers will be taken forward from this PSQ to participate in the Invitation to Tender (ITT). 
The stage 2 evaluation scores and weightings are detailed within the PSQ Assessment Methodology Document. An individual weighted score is calculated for each question by multiplying the question weighting by the appropriate score allocated to the Potential Provider for that question. A total weighted score is then calculated by adding together the entire individual question weighted scores for the Potential Provider.
The Potential Provider’s response to each question shall be evaluated in accordance with the Potential Provider selection criteria detailed in the PSQ Assessment Methodology Document. 
All questions must be answered without reference to general marketing or promotional material. 
No more than five Potential Providers will be taken forward from this PSQ to participate in the Invitation to Tender (ITT). 
The exercise will be conducted in the English language. If any of the required information (e.g. text in financial accounts) is not available in English, please supply a copy of the original document and an English translation of that information. 
A maximum of five Potential Providers will be shortlisted from this PSQ stage to proceed to the Invitation to Tender (ITT).
Only Potential Providers who:
a.	Achieve a ‘pass’ rating on all pass/fail questions, and
b.	Meet or exceed the minimum required standards for economic and financial standing, as well as technical or professional ability, as set out in the Authority’s pre-qualification criteria;
will be invited to submit a tender.
If more than five Potential Providers satisfy the above criteria, only the top five Potential Providers with the highest overall evaluation scores will progress to the ITT.
The Authority reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to obtain independent financial and market advice to verify the accuracy of information provided by Potential Providers or to assist in any aspect of the pre-qualification evaluation.

tender.title: WNC Security Services - Core Guarding
tender.description:
West Northamptonshire Council (WNC) requires the provision of professional Manned Guarding Services across its estate. Services will be delivered at a range of Council-owned and managed premises, including high-profile, public-facing locations.
The effective delivery of these services is critical to maintaining the security of Council premises and ensuring the safety and wellbeing of Council employees, contractors, service users, visitors, vulnerable individuals, children, and members of the public. WNC require a reliable, customer-focused and professional security service, operating across a variety of sites with shift patterns ranging up to 12 hours and covering requirements of up to 24 hours per day, 7 days per week.
They shall demonstrate robust recruitment, screening and vetting procedures and ensure that all security personnel, hold the appropriate current Security Industry Authority (SIA) licences and accreditations relevant to their role and are subject to enhanced recruitment checks, including DBS checks where required.
•	The Service Provider shall ensure ongoing training and professional development for all personnel assigned to the Contract. 
•	The Service Provider shall maintain a pool of appropriately trained and authorised relief staff capable of covering planned and unplanned absence. 
•	The Service Provider must provide assurance that service continuity, security standards and contractual obligations will be maintained at all times.
tender.procurementMethodRationale:
The Council determined that continuation of the existing contractual arrangements was no longer appropriate.The resulting requirement to secure replacement security services at short notice has created a situation of extreme and unavoidable urgency.The need to secure immediate replacement security provision was not reasonably foreseeable and has arisen from the occurrence of recent service incidents rather than any act or omission of the Council.
The Council must ensure that appropriate security arrangements are in place immediately upon termination of the existing contract in order to avoid any gap in service provision which would create unacceptable risk of interruption to service.
Any interruption to security provision would create unacceptable risks to public safety, the security of Council employees, members of the public, Council property and other assets. West Northamptonshire Council requires the uninterrupted provision of security guarding services across a number of operational, public-facing and critical Council sites.
The Council therefore considers it strictly necessary to implement replacement arrangements without delay in order to ensure continuity of security services and maintain appropriate security coverage across its estate.
The direct award is considered strictly necessary for a 12-month term to ensure continuity of critical services, allow for sufficient time for mobilisation, operational stabilisation, implementation of the replacement arrangements and completion of a longer-term compliant competitive procurement exercise.
The Council has considered a shorter contract duration but concluded that a shorter period would create a significant risk of procurement activity needing to commence before service delivery has stabilised following transition from the incumbent provider.
The contract does not include extension options and is intended solely as an interim arrangement pending implementation of a longer-term procurement solution.
The Council does not have sufficient time to undertake a competitive procurement process, including an accelerated competitive procedure available for urgent competitive procedures under section 54(3)-(4) of the Procurement Act 2023, before replacement arrangements are required.
A direct award is therefore being made pursuant to section 41 and paragraph 13 of Schedule 5 of the Procurement Act 2023 on the basis that it is strictly necessary on the grounds of extreme and unavoidable urgency.
1st Reaction has been identified as a supplier capable of mobilising within the required timescales and maintaining continuity of service. Currently they are delivering services to the Council Lot 4 - out of hours, monitoring and maintenance provision. The supplier possesses the operational capability, local knowledge, infrastructure and resources required to mobilise and deliver the services from commencement of the contract with minimal disruption to service delivery.

tender.title: Continued UK Contribution to the MicroCarb Mission – CO₂ Retrieval Algorithm Development and Programme Support
tender.description:
The MicroCarb mission is a Centre National d'Études Spatiales (CNES) led satellite mission designed to deliver high-precision measurements of atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO₂). The United Kingdom contributes to the mission through scientific, technical and validation activities coordinated by UK Space Agency (UKSA) and delivered via UK partners.
This contract covers the continuation of activities required to support the UK contribution for the remainder of FY 2026–27, with a particular focus on continued CO₂ retrieval algorithm development, post-launch data exploitation, and ongoing programme-level technical engagement within the MicroCarb mission framework. The services under this contract will continue the development and application of CO₂ retrieval algorithms, preparation for the ingestion and processing of MicroCarb data products provided by CNES, and coordination of UK expertise through continued participation in the MicroCarb Advisory Group (MAG). The work builds upon progress delivered to date in providing mission-specific technical support, including adaptation of NASA-developed retrieval frameworks and preparatory activities supporting the transition of MicroCarb towards an operational data exploitation phase. Activities will place increased emphasis on algorithm robustness, data handling capability, validation readiness and sustained mission engagement.
Activities under this contract would include:
CO₂ Retrieval Algorithm Development and Assessment - Incorporation of prior information modules (ABO2 and GASBAG) and a meteorological pre-processor (GEOS-IT) into the CO₂ retrieval pipeline; adaptation of existing NASA-developed software to operate with synthetic MicroCarb data for the standard three spectral bands; Development of capability to ingest and utilise the fourth MicroCarb spectral band (1.27 µm) and assessment of its performance; Assessment of preliminary MicroCarb Level 2 retrieval performance, including preparation for comparison with CNES retrieval products.
MicroCarb Advisory Group and Programme Support - Representation of UKSA/DSIT within the MicroCarb Advisory Group (MAG); Liaison with UK and French partners, including CNES; Provision of technical and programme-level updates and reporting; and submission of a summary report of activities undertaken.
